The basics

What is pediatric occupational therapy?

A child's "occupations" are the everyday things they need and want to do: playing, getting dressed, eating, sleeping, learning, and spending time with family and friends. Pediatric occupational therapy helps kids take part in those things in ways that work for their body and brain.

Our goal is to help each child feel comfortable, confident, and able to join in on their own terms, without masking who they are.

How we help

Areas we support

Every child is different, so therapy is built around your child's strengths and your family's goals. These are some of the areas families come to us for.

Sensory processing

Helping your child take in and respond to sights, sounds, textures, and movement so everyday places feel more comfortable.

Fine motor & handwriting

Building hand strength and control for writing, drawing, cutting, buttons, zippers, and utensils.

Self-care & daily routines

Growing independence with dressing, toileting, brushing teeth, bathing, and getting out the door.

Feeding & mealtimes

Gentle, pressure-free support for picky eating and making meals feel calmer for the whole family.

Emotional regulation

Noticing big feelings and body signals, and building tools that help your child feel safe and in control.

Motor planning & coordination

Coordinating the body for play, playground equipment, sports, balance, and everyday movement.

Attention & executive function

Support with focus, transitions, planning, and multi-step routines at home and school.

Play & social connection

Joining in, taking turns, and building friendships in ways that feel authentic to your child.

Getting started

From first call to real progress

Here's how strengths-based, neurodiversity-affirming care turns into a plan your family can actually live with.

Step 1

Free phone consult

A no-pressure call to talk about your child and see whether we're the right fit.

Step 2

Play-based evaluation

A relaxed, child-led session to understand your child's strengths and where support helps. It may include standardized assessments and parent questionnaires.

Step 3

A plan built on strengths

Goals we set together, around your family's routines, priorities, and your child's interests.

Step 4

Grow together

Ongoing sessions at home, in the community, in office, or by telehealth, with progress you can see.

Our approach

Play-based, child-led, and affirming

Child-led and strengths-based

We follow your child's lead and start with what they can do, never from a list of deficits. When play feels like theirs, real growth follows.

DIR Floortime in every session

We weave DIR Floortime, a relationship-based approach, into therapy with every child and coach parents to use it at home. Learn about DIR Floortime

Good to know

Occupational therapy questions, answered

Do you take insurance for occupational therapy?
We're in-network with Blue Cross Blue Shield, TennCare Select, and BlueCare. For other plans, we offer private pay (card, cash, or HSA) and can provide a superbill to submit for reimbursement. Katie Beckett Waiver and IEA funding may also apply. We're also a TEIS (Tennessee Early Intervention System) provider for children from birth to age 3.
Are you a TEIS provider?
Yes. Cultivate Play is a provider with TEIS (Tennessee Early Intervention System), which serves children from birth to age 3 with developmental delays or disabilities. If your child is enrolled in TEIS, ask your service coordinator about receiving services with us.
Do we need a referral from our doctor?
The easiest first step is a free phone consultation. We'll talk about your child and family and whether we're the right fit. Prefer to skip the call? Have your pediatrician fax a referral to (615) 617-5873 and we'll take it from there.
Where do OT sessions happen?
In your home or community across Rutherford County (Murfreesboro, Smyrna, La Vergne, and nearby), in our Murfreesboro office at 1810 Ward Drive, or by telehealth anywhere in Tennessee.
What ages do you work with?
Children and teens, ages 0 to 18.
What happens at the first evaluation?
The evaluation is a relaxed, child-led play session. We get to know your child, learn what's going well and what feels hard, and talk with you about your family's priorities. Depending on your child's needs, it may also include standardized assessments and questionnaires for you to fill out, which help us understand your child more fully. Then we set goals together.
Do you work with autistic children?
Yes. We are a neurodiversity-affirming practice, and many of the children we see are autistic, ADHD, or both. We support things like sensory needs, regulation, daily routines, and play in ways that respect how your child's brain works.
